::: {.callout-note .se-question appearance="simple"}
## The question

[Bundle packages with a document](https://tex.stackexchange.com/questions/14520/bundle-packages-with-a-document), asked by [Hooked](https://tex.stackexchange.com/users/352/hooked) on TeX Stack Exchange (2011-03-29; [CC BY-SA 2.5](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/2.5/)):

> I'd like to have my LaTeX document be self-contained, that is, if I move to another computer I'd like all of my non-standard packages to work without first installing them. For simple enough packages I can put the `.sty` files into the base directory, but this seems like a clunky solution. I can put the packages in a subdirectory but I sometimes than I get dependency errors like
>
> ```latex
>  LaTeX Warning: You have requested package style_files/placeins
>  but the package provides `placeins'.
>
>  (/usr/share/texmf-texlive/tex/latex/tools/array.sty)
> ```
>
> Is there a right way (tm) to do this, or should I install every package I need on every computer I use?
:::

Take a look at Scott Pakin's scripts on CTAN under [`bundledoc`](http://www.ctan.org/tex-archive/support/bundledoc/).  `bundledoc` is a perl script that gathers all the dependent files to processing a single file and puts them in a single directory, then zips it up for easy transport.
